notes: Comprehension: 'mud' is not glossed but carries the punchline; consider adding it to the glossed key words or adding a short clue ('some wet, brown mud').
Comprehension: 'laws' in 'The other knew all the laws.' could be 'all the rules of the town' for true beginners.
'On the way, he found an old crow.' In Andersen the crow is dead; 'old crow' may make a learner picture a live bird that is then cooked. 'a dead crow' is still gentle and clearer.

'Yes, because my father cooks chickens,' is slightly unnatural (habitual present for an action happening now). Within the present-simple limit, 'Yes. There is a big fire. My father cooks chickens today.' or 'Yes. The cooks make chickens for my father.' reads a little better.
'Yes, because my father cooks young chickens today,' - present simple with 'today' sounds slightly off to a native ear; acceptable under the level's tense limit.
'We want to talk our way to her.' is a slightly clipped idiom; 'We want to win her with our words.' is clearer for A2.
'We are going to talk our way to the princess.' - 'talk our way into the princess's heart' (as in B2) or 'win the princess with our words' is more idiomatic.
No conditionals or passive found; the alderman episode and the unreliable-newspaper ending are kept, which is faithful to Andersen.
'braces' is British for suspenders; fine, but learners using US English may not know it in this sense.

Faithful and genuinely literary (the 'half their cleverness' opening, the 'nobody had ever really counted the third one' aside, the ink blots, the untrustworthy paper). Omitting Hans's cheeky 'and if she won't have me, I'll have her anyway' is a reasonable softening.

summary: A faithful retelling of Andersen's 'Clod Hans' at every level: the learned brothers, the goat, the crow/clog/mud gifts, the roasting-chickens exchange, and (from B1 up) the clerks, the alderman and the unreliable newspaper ending. Grammar limits are respected, quizzes have single defensible answers, and nothing breaches 4+ suitability. Only minor taste notes remain, chiefly glossing 'mud' and saying 'dead crow' at A1.
